title: Since God does not cause sin in time, his will is no cause of sin's futurity; it depends only on his decree to permit
source_text: LVIII. Cum ergo Deus in tempore causa peccati non sit, tantum abest ut dicendum putem Dei voluntatem esse causam unicam futuritionis peccati, ut plane & simpliciter negandum existimem illam esse istius futuritionis causam, vel solam, vel cum causa secunda. Verum est quidem hominem non peccare, nisi dependenter a Dei voluntate. Nec enim peccare posset, nisi Deus ipsum peccare permitteret. Et sic quoque peccati futuritio pendet a decreto Dei de peccato permittendo. Sed quemadmodum Dei voluntas non propterea dicenda est propria causa cur homo actu peccet; sic etiam inde non sequitur Dei decretum esse propriam causam futuritionis peccati.
pass_a_gloss: LVIII. Since therefore God is not the cause of sin in time, so far am I from thinking it should be said that the will of God is the only cause of the futurition of sin, that I judge it must plainly & simply be denied that it is the cause of that futurition, either alone, or with the second cause. It is true indeed that man does not sin, except dependently on the will of God. For he could not sin, unless God permitted him to sin. And thus also the futurition of sin depends on the decree of God concerning permitting sin. But just as the will of God is not on that account to be called the proper cause why man actually sins; so also it does not follow thence that the decree of God is the proper cause of the futurition of sin.
pass_b_english: Since God is not the cause of sin in time, I am far from thinking we should say that God's will is the only cause of sin's futurity. On the contrary, I judge that we must deny plainly and without qualification that it is the cause of that futurity at all, whether on its own or together with the second cause.
It is true that man sins only in dependence on God's will, since he could not sin unless God permitted him to. In that sense the futurity of sin also depends on God's decree to permit sin.
But God's will is not for that reason to be called the proper cause of man's actually sinning. In the same way, it does not follow that God's decree is the proper cause of the futurity of sin.
